name: Learn basic video editing
blurb: Cutting, pacing, audio and export settings. The technical part of editing is a week; the judgement about when to cut is the actual skill.
gear: Footage — your own, or free stock
steps: Learn the interface and the basic operations: import, timeline, trim, ripple delete, and keyboard shortcuts.
Learn to assemble a rough cut fast without perfecting anything, then refine — editing forwards in perfect order wastes enormous time.
Learn J-cuts and L-cuts, where audio leads or trails the picture. This one technique makes amateur edits look professional.
Learn audio: level matching, ducking music under speech, and removing background noise. Bad audio reads as amateur faster than bad picture.
Learn basic colour correction, then grading, and keep them as separate steps.
Learn export settings for the platform you are targeting, and finish something short and complete.
tips: Cut on motion and cut earlier than feels comfortable. Beginner edits are almost always too slow.
Fix audio before you touch colour. Viewers forgive bad picture long before bad sound.
proof: A finished two-minute video with clean cuts, balanced audio and a consistent look.
